# CI, ported from vira.hs (Vira <https://vira.nixos.asia/>).
#
# Same coverage as before: the four flakes devoured (srid/devour-flake — what
# Vira itself uses to build a flake), with the same input overrides, built for
# x86_64-linux and aarch64-darwin (via the matrix). The Vira "signoff" check
# is replaced by this workflow's own check runs across the matrix (one
# `devour-flake (os, subflake)` per combination), and the build cache by
# `cache-nix-action` (store cache persisted across runs).
name: ci

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:

jobs:
  devour-flake:
    name: "devour-flake (${{ matrix.os }}, ${{ matrix.flake.name }})"
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os:
          # build.systems in the old vira.hs
          - ubuntu-latest # x86_64-linux
          - macos-latest  # aarch64-darwin
        flake:
          # build.flakes (with overrideInputs) in the old vira.hs. nix input
          # path suffix is relative to the repo root ($PWD); the subflake path
          # is relative to the root too.
          - name: crate-parser
            path: nix/crate-parser/test
            input: crate-parser
            inputPath: /nix/crate-parser
          - name: dev
            path: dev
            input: rust-flake
            inputPath: ""
          - name: single-crate
            path: examples/single-crate
            input: rust-flake
            inputPath: ""
          - name: multi-crate
            path: examples/multi-crate
            input: rust-flake
            inputPath: ""
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write # cache-nix-action's purge: true requires it
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: nixbuild/nix-quick-install-action@v34
      - uses: nix-community/cache-nix-action@v6
        with:
          primary-key: nix-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/flake.lock') }}
          restore-prefixes-first-match: nix-${{ runner.os }}-
          gc-max-store-size-linux: 5G
          gc-max-store-size-macos: 5G
          purge: true
          purge-prefixes: nix-${{ runner.os }}-
          purge-last-accessed: 604800
          purge-primary-key: never

      # Devour the subflake exactly how Vira builds it (see
      # packages/devour-flake/src/DevourFlake.hs in juspay/vira): builds every
      # package, check, devShell, app, ... of the flake for the current system.
      - name: "devour ${{ matrix.flake.name }}"
        run: >
          nix build github:srid/devour-flake#default -L --print-out-paths
          --no-write-lock-file --no-link
          --override-input flake "path:$PWD/${{ matrix.flake.path }}"
          --override-input "flake/${{ matrix.flake.input }}" "path:$PWD${{ matrix.flake.inputPath }}"

name: update-flake-lock
on:
  workflow_dispatch: # allows manual triggering
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 0 * * 0' # runs weekly on Sunday at 00:00

jobs:
  example-lock:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install Nix
        uses: DeterminateSystems/nix-installer-action@main
      - name: Update flake.lock
        uses: DeterminateSystems/update-flake-lock@main
        with:
          commit-msg: "nix: Update flake.lock"
          pr-title: "Update flake.lock"
          pr-labels: |
            automated
          branch: "update_flake_lock"
      - name: Enable auto-merge
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          pr=$(gh pr list --head update_flake_lock --state open --json number --jq '.[0].number')
          [ -n "$pr" ] && gh pr merge "$pr" --auto --squash || echo "no PR to auto-merge"

# rust-flake

A simple flake module for Rust development, based on [Crane](https://crane.dev/). `rust-flake` is inspired by [`haskell-flake`](https://github.com/srid/haskell-flake).

## Examples

- Single crates
    - https://github.com/srid/rust-nix-template
    - https://github.com/juspay/nix-rs
- Multi-crate workspace
    - https://github.com/juspay/omnix
    - https://github.com/juspay/superposition
- Desktop apps
    - https://github.com/srid/dioxus-desktop-template
    - https://github.com/juspay/omnix

## Comparison with other tools

| | rust-flake | [nix-cargo-integration](https://github.com/yusdacra/nix-cargo-integration) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stable over time | ✔️ | ✖️[^crane] |

[^crane]: `rust-flake` uses [crane](https://crane.dev/) directly, which is known to be stable. Whereas `nix-cargo-integration` uses `dream2nix` which is known to be unstable. See [here](https://matrix.to/#/!gcrYWdPsIUOFpXFDHB:matrix.org/$vJGlKFLKj4uRp-QkokK_0ISnnXHaXQ5tv7A_PcDYl7A?via=matrix.org&via=nixos.dev&via=goblin.sh) and [here](https://github.com/srid/rust-nix-template/pull/27)

# `crate-parser`
**crate-parser** provides parsers for Rust-associated files.

## Features

- Currently, the main available function is [`findCrates`](./default.nix), which processes `workspace.members` globs from `Cargo.toml`.

For example:
```toml
[workspace]
members = [ "crates/*" ]
````

This will be handled correctly by `findCrates`, resolving the paths accordingly.

## Contributing

Feel free to create a PR to improve **crate-parser** — contributions are welcome!
